original.target_description: Primary source examined; multiple p. 5 CFA model fit and difference tests are consistent with the broad locator, especially section 4.2 worry/rumination/reflection extension analyses. Row-specific target unresolved.

notes: Identity verified from supplied canonical text: title A bifactor approach to modeling the structure of repetitive thinking: Replication and extension; authors Ariana A. Castro, Juyoen Hur, Howard Berenbaum; Personality and Individual Differences 189 (2022) 111472; DOI 10.1016/j.paid.2021.111472. Primary published research report with Methods, Results, tables and References across nine printed pages, not an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF path supplied; no PDF rendered. All assigned inputs have the same study label, broad description and p. 5 locator. They do not distinguish any particular model comparison or goodness-of-fit test. No mapping to audit IDs can be established without assigning by row order or numeric matching. Most directly aligned candidates including reflection: p. 5, section 4.2: content-specific versus single-factor, printed ΔX2(3) = 35,419.8, p < .001; valence bifactor versus content-specific, printed ΔX2(26) = 1163.1, p < .001; content-specific bifactor versus valence bifactor, printed ΔX2(11) = 2302.6, p < .001. Each p bound belongs to its stated difference test (bound l, value .001); no row-specific selection made. Table 3 also prints five model goodness-of-fit X2 statistics: single factor 43,822.59 (df 740), content-specific 8402.85 (df 737), valence 17,397.17 (df 739), content-specific bifactor 4937.13 (df 700), valence bifactor 7239.72 (df 711). No corresponding p is printed in Table 3. p. 5 section 4.1 additionally gives worry/rumination-only comparison candidates: PSWQ/RRQ ΔX2(1) = 12,275.56 and ΔX2(27) = 1491.74; PSWQ/RSQ ΔX2(1) = 25,538.6 and ΔX2(37) = 12,186.74, all p < .001. These omit reflection and are not silently substituted. Model-level N candidate: 2428 participants for extension CFA (p. 4 section 3.2 and p. 5 Table 3); printed directly, no arithmetic. Table 1 N = 2091 for PSWQ/RRQ worry/rumination replication analyses (p. 4 footnote 2 excludes Hur et al. 2017 data); Table 2 N = 2256 for PSWQ/RSQ. Whole-paper item-data N = 4711 is not assigned as analytic N. Missing-data/exclusion details for extension CFA are not explicitly resolved here; p. 4 pairwise-present description is in SEM factor validity analysis. Since the row-specific target remains ambiguous, N = 2428 is retained only as a common-model candidate for parent field-scope review, as instructed. No summed N or effect conversion performed. Candidate verbatim evidence (ordered canonical fragments): ΔX2(3) = 35,419.8, p < .001 ... ΔX2(26) = 1163.1, p < .001 ... ΔX2(11) = 2302.6, p < .001. Unassigned replication and reported_success are placeholders only. Original side done means source review completed, not that the ambiguous row target was matched.
